tool.name: Build haplotype sheet
tool.description: collect window haplotype calls into a PyEuk sheet, keeping read frequency
tool.command: ## Reduces the whole collection: the sheet only means anything across specimens. ## Element identifiers are sanitised into filenames, but the specimen id itself is ## read from each file's own 'specimen' column, never from the filename. mkdir -p calls && #import re #for $c in $calls_in ln -s '$c' 'calls/${re.sub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", str($c.element_identifier))}.tsv' && #end for pyeuk build-sheet calls out --min-freq $min_freq --min-reads $min_reads --min-maf $min_maf && cp out/sheet.tsv '$sheet' && cp out/haplotype_map.tsv '$hapmap' && cp out/calls_long.tsv '$calls_long' && cp out/dropped_columns.tsv '$dropped'

param.name: min_freq
param.label: Extra haplotype-frequency filter
param.help: On top of whatever the caller already applied. 0 keeps everything.

param.name: min_maf
param.label: Minor-allele filter
param.help: Drop a haplotype column unless it is carried by at least this fraction of the specimens called at its window (and at most 1 minus it). 0 disables. THIS IS LOAD-BEARING: PyEuk weights a column 1/sqrt(p(1-p)), which is minimised at p=0.5 and diverges as p approaches 0, so it weights rare alleles most heavily. On a 153-specimen sheet, 17 columns carried by 2 or fewer specimens held 79.6% of all weight and the encoding scored ARI -0.0057; filtering at 0.05 gave 0.9734. Note p is a fraction of SPECIMENS, not reads, so within-specimen minor haplotypes in a mixture are untouched.

data.name: dropped
data.label: ${tool.name}: columns removed by the minor-allele filter

tool.help:
A column is one observed haplotype string in one window, named ``<window>_Hap_<i>`` so that PyEuk's locus grouping (which strips exactly that suffix) treats each window as its own locus window. The content-derived name lives in the map output.
Two properties follow from naming by content rather than by catalogue:
* "amplified and reference-identical" is the ordinary haplotype ``=``, a positive observation, so no special CALLED column is needed and a reference-identical specimen is not confusable with a dropout. * a mixture is several haplotypes in one window, represented natively.
The long-format output keeps read counts and frequencies, which the binary sheet cannot carry.
